newsitem.title: INDIA: Pakistan says Kashmir key in talks with India.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan says Kashmir key in talks with India.

text.p: Pakistan looks forward to resolving outstanding issues in talks with India, particularly a longstanding dispute over the Himalayan region of Kashmir, Pakistani Foreign Secretary Shamshad Ahmad said on Thursday.

"We are absolutely clear that there is an urgent need to meaningfully address all outstanding issues, particularly the core issue of Jammu and Kashmir," Ahmad said on arrival in the Indian capital for four days of talks scheduled to start on Friday.

Ahmad and his Indian counterpart Salman Haidar are scheduled to resume talks broken off three years ago mainly over the thorny issue of Kashmir where a seven-year-old Moslem separatist movement has taken ties between the neighbours to a new low.

Ahmad said "(the) time is propitious for us to seize this opportunity for removing the root causes of tension between Pakistan and India" and added Islamabad hoped its "sincerity of purpose" would be reciprocated by New Delhi.
The two neighbours have gone to war twice over Kashmir since independence from Britain in 1947.
